solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American ship left Spain following essentially pointless skirmish

indicators.note: the ship, left and Spain come after the central letter, so they follow it in the answer
the essence of a word is its very centre, so take the middle letter of pointless

parts.note: middle letter T of this nine-letter word
USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A pointless naval spat between a US vessel and Spain that ends in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: The ninth-letter word pointless has T at its heart; then USS, L and E follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous struggle or scuffle, a close synonym of a skirmish.

clue.text: Crate mostly containing top of range whisky

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the shortened crate goes round the letter
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tea chest is a large wooden crate

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means its first letter

parts.note: first letter R

explanation.surface: Most of a box holds a premium bottle of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA CHEST loses its last letter to make TEACHES, and R goes inside. Teacher's is a well-known brand of Scotch whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacher's is a brand name of blended Scotch, so an example of a whisky.

clue.text: Bird from Norway captivated by melancholy musician

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so Norway sits within melancholy

parts.note: sad means melancholy
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
a piper is a musician

explanation.surface: A Norwegian bird is enthralled by a mournful player.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a wading shorebird with a long slender bill.

clue.text: Unknown factor in non-clerical types' negligence

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the lay people

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown element explains why lay folk are careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or lack of care, a near synonym of negligence.

clue.text: Philosophical treatise written by graduate about society

indicators.note: the treatise comes after the graduate and society, as a text is signed by its writer
about here means turned round, so the graduate's letters run backwards

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: An academic paper on social theory produced by a fresh graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosophical treatise' reads as one phrase, but only 'Philosophical' is the definition; 'treatise' is TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract thought is theoretical rather than concrete, the kind of reasoning philosophy deals in.

clue.text: Family died partaking in winter sport? Horrific!

parts.note: blood means family or kin

indicators.note: partaking in means taking part inside, so died goes into the sport

parts.note: curling is played on ice with stones
D is the genealogy abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A relative dies while playing a sport on ice: how dreadful!
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodcurdling means terrifying, causing horror enough to chill the blood.

clue.text: Oddly, Tory measure is best

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters, first and third of Tory

parts.note: an ounce is a measure of weight

explanation.surface: Strangely, a Conservative policy proves the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is the verb to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them soundly, which is to best them.

clue.text: A tragic heroine upheld virtue

indicators.note: upheld in a down clue means lifted up, so the heroine's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: A doomed heroine is credited with moral goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable quality, so a virtue in the sense of a merit.

clue.text: Commotion engulfing large English city

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the commotion wraps the other letters

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A disturbance overwhelms a big English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English city' tempts as the definition, but Toledo is in Spain (or Ohio); English gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, also one in Ohio.

clue.text: A former partner is said to be appropriate

indicators.note: is said tells us to listen to the phrase spoken rather than read it

parts.note: a former partner is an ex, so the phrase is 'an ex'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is fitting to call an old flame a suitable match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to take it over for oneself, the verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Expert tricks extremely uncivil govenor

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
cons are swindles or tricks

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters U and L

explanation.surface: A rude colonial governor gets up to devious tricks like a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'govenor', a slip for governor. In ancient Rome a proconsul governed a province.
explanation.definitionFit: A proconsul was the Roman official who administered a province, so a provincial ruler.

clue.text: Coin collectors cruelly pestering Mark

indicators.note: cruelly suggests rough handling, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Numismatists harass someone named Mark without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin collectors' suggests numismatists, but the machines collect coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Parking meters take coins as payment for parking time, so they literally gather coins.

clue.text: Trendy joint starts to earn reputation on street

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: first letter E
first letter R

explanation.surface: A fashionable venue begins to win a name for itself on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trendy joint' looks like a fashionable bar; 'joint' actually belongs to the wordplay as HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster is a person who follows the latest fashions; used here loosely as a noun for one who is trendy.

clue.text: Gifted crime boss dined with Democrat

parts.note: a don is a Mafia boss
ate means dined
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A talented mobster shares a meal with a Democratic politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' reads as talented but means given away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted in the sense of handed over as a present means donated.

clue.text: Mellow river that is crossing Portugal

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the river and that is go round Portugal

parts.note: IE, id est, is Latin for that is
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A gentle river flowing across Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe fruit or cheese is fully matured, soft and rich, which is what mellow describes.

clue.text: Defending regime in TV broadcast is extremely harmful

indicators.note: defending means surrounding something to shield it, so the scrambled letters go round the regime
broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of in and TV are rearranged

parts.note: a regime is a system of rule

explanation.surface: Propaganda supporting a regime on television is damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged IN and TV give VINT, which goes around RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulent describes a disease or poison that is severely damaging, very harmful indeed.

clue.text: Blend of ten rustic flavours

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A mixture of ten country-style tastes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinctures are tinges or traces, so a slight flavour or tint of something.

clue.text: Vision certainly embraced by rowing team

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so certainly goes within the rowing team

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is certainly hugging a clear view.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, i.e. vision.

clue.text: Lesson about Scandinavian revolutionary protecting East German dissident

indicators.note: about means around, so the lesson wraps the rest

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school lesson

indicators.note: protecting means sheltering inside, so the reversed Scandinavian goes round East German
revolutionary means turning round, so the Scandinavian is read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is from Denmark

explanation.surface: A class about a Danish radical who shelters an East German defector.
explanation.walkthrough: DANE reversed is ENAD; E and G go inside it to make ENEGAD, which RE then wraps. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a party or cause, as a dissident breaks with the established order.

clue.text: New uniform meets with unambiguous sort of reaction

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
clear means unambiguous

explanation.surface: A fresh dress code is greeted with a clear-cut response.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reaction is one in atomic nuclei, so nuclear names a kind of reaction.

clue.text: Resent two letters, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so we hear the letters' names

parts.note: the letters N and V, said 'en vee'

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at a pair of letters they have heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy someone is to feel resentful longing for what they have.

clue.text: High-pitched sound of note held in Beat It

indicators.note: held in means kept inside, so the note sits within the command

parts.note: scram means beat it, go away
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A high note sung in Michael Jackson's Beat It.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat It' looks like the song title but is the command to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry, a shrill high-pitched sound.

clue.text: Penny gets in pickle for partner

indicators.note: gets in means enters, so the penny goes inside the pickle

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine

explanation.surface: A coin drops into a jar of pickle meant for one's other half.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a husband or wife, one's marriage partner.

clue.text: Stall inexperienced reporter, caught in elaborate lie

parts.note: a cub reporter is a novice journalist

indicators.note: in places caught inside the rearranged lie
elaborate means intricately worked, so the letters of lie are reworked

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rookie journalist is caught out in a complicated falsehood and plays for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a verb (delay) but is a noun: a booth. LIE rearranged gives ILE, with C put in to make ICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned compartment, like a stall in a stable or washroom.

clue.text: Bust crown of skull in explosion

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the explosion

parts.note: a boom is the sound of an explosion

indicators.note: the crown is the top, and in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter S

explanation.surface: A sculpted head breaks the top of a skull in a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a verb (break) but is the noun for chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and bosom both refer to a woman's chest.

clue.text: Steerpike's favourite just discovered motivation

parts.note: Steerpike is the setter, so 'Steerpike's' means I'm
a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover stripped, so the outer letters of just go

parts.note: remove J and T to leave US

explanation.surface: The setter's beloved has only just been found, giving a push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like found, but it means uncovered: take the first and last letters off JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that moves something on, a synonym of motivation.

clue.text: Improvised reggae set is unexpected bonus

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: An impromptu reggae performance turns out to be a pleasant surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is a hidden extra feature in software, film or games, a surprise treat.

clue.text: Remove tackle from river in college grounds, primarily

indicators.note: in places the river inside the college

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of grounds

explanation.surface: Fishing gear must be cleared out of a river on university land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' suggests fishing gear but means a ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of its rigging, the ropes and gear called tackle.

clue.text: Learn from cultural reference involving old retired nobleman

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the cultural reference goes round the rest

parts.note: a meme is a cultural idea or reference passed around

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the nobleman's title is reversed

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight or baronet

explanation.surface: A student picks something up from an in-joke about an aged retired lord.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR reversed is RIS; with O before it, ORIS goes inside MEME.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise something is to commit it to memory, i.e. learn it by heart.

clue.text: Prepare to run twisted experiment, say

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: a test is an experiment
EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A tangled trial gets ready to start, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST followed by EG reads TESTEG, and reversed it gives the answer. 'Twisted' tempts as an anagram signal, but a full reversal is what works.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Get set' is the middle command of a race start, telling runners to be ready to go.
